passages.text: Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field that the LORD God had made. And he said to the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden?’ ”
passages.sermon:
The serpent was a creature.
The LORD God made the serpent.
The serpent was more crafty than any other animal in the field.
The serpent spoke to the woman.
The serpent asked the woman a question.
The serpent said, “Did God really say you must not eat from any tree in the garden?”
passages.original: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ף כִּֽי־ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן׃

passages.text: The woman answered the serpent, “We may eat the fruit of the trees of the garden, but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God has said, ‘You must not eat of it or touch it, or you will die.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The woman spoke to the serpent.
She said, “We may eat the fruit from the trees in the garden.
But there is a tree in the middle of the garden.
God said about that tree, ‘Do not eat its fruit.
Do not touch it.
If you do, you will die.’”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־ הַנָּחָ֑שׁ מִפְּרִ֥י עֵֽץ־ הַגָּ֖ן נֹאכֵֽל׃ וּמִפְּרִ֣י הָעֵץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתוֹךְ־ הַגָּן֒ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְלֹ֥א תִגְּע֖וּ בּ֑וֹ פֶּן־ תְּמֻתֽוּן׃

passages.text: “You will not surely die,” the serpent told her.
passages.sermon: The serpent was more crafty than any animal that the LORD God had made.\r\nThe serpent spoke to the woman.\r\nThe serpent said to the woman, “You will not surely die.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַנָּחָ֖שׁ אֶל־ הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה לֹֽא־ מ֖וֹת תְּמֻתֽוּן׃

passages.text: “For God knows that in the day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”
passages.sermon:
The serpent spoke to the woman.
The serpent said that God knows something important.
God knows what will happen if you eat from the tree.
On the day you eat from the tree, your eyes will be opened.
You will become like God.
You will know good and evil.
passages.original: כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכָלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶם֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים יֹדְעֵ֖י ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע׃

passages.text: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eyes, and that it was desirable for obtaining wisdom, she took the fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.
passages.sermon:
The woman saw the tree.
She saw that the tree was good for food.
She saw that the tree was pleasing to the eyes.
She saw that the tree was desirable for gaining wisdom.
She took fruit from the tree.
She ate the fruit.
Her husband was with her.
She gave some fruit to her husband.
He ate the fruit.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֣רֶא הָֽאִשָּׁ֡ה כִּ֣י טוֹב֩ הָעֵ֨ץ לְמַאֲכָ֜ל וְכִ֧י תַֽאֲוָה־ ה֣וּא לָעֵינַ֗יִם וְנֶחְמָ֤ד הָעֵץ֙ לְהַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַתִּקַּ֥ח מִפִּרְי֖וֹ וַתֹּאכַ֑ל וַתִּתֵּ֧ן גַּם־ לְאִישָׁ֛הּ עִמָּ֖הּ וַיֹּאכַֽל׃

passages.text: And the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves.
passages.sermon:
Adam and his wife ate the fruit from the tree.
God had told them not to eat from this tree.
After they ate, both of their eyes were opened.
They realized they were naked.
They took fig leaves.
They sewed the fig leaves together.
They made coverings for themselves.
passages.original: וַתִּפָּקַ֙חְנָה֙ עֵינֵ֣י שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י עֵֽירֻמִּ֖ם הֵ֑ם וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ֙ עֲלֵ֣ה תְאֵנָ֔ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם חֲגֹרֹֽת׃

passages.text: Then the man and his wife heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the breeze of the day, and they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
passages.sermon:
The LORD God is the Creator.
The LORD God walked in the garden.
The day was cool and breezy.
The man and his wife were in the garden.
The man and his wife heard the voice of the LORD God.
The man and his wife hid themselves.
They hid from the presence of the LORD God.
They hid among the trees of the garden.
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶת־ ק֨וֹל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּגָּ֖ן לְר֣וּחַ הַיּ֑וֹם וַיִּתְחַבֵּ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם וְאִשְׁתּ֗וֹ מִפְּנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן׃

passages.text: But the LORD God called out to the man, “Where are you?”
passages.sermon: The LORD God is the Creator.\r\nThe LORD God called to the man.\r\nThe LORD God said to the man, “Where are you?”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֛א יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־ הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ אַיֶּֽכָּה׃

passages.text: “I heard Your voice in the garden,” he replied, “and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself.”
passages.sermon:
Adam was the first man.
Adam spoke to the LORD God.
Adam said, “I heard Your voice in the garden.”
Adam said, “I was afraid.”
Adam said, “I was naked.”
Adam said, “So I hid myself.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֶת־ קֹלְךָ֥ שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בַּגָּ֑ן וָאִירָ֛א כִּֽי־ עֵירֹ֥ם אָנֹ֖כִי וָאֵחָבֵֽא׃

passages.text: “Who told you that you were naked?” asked the LORD God. “Have you eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?”
passages.sermon:
The LORD God spoke to the man.
The LORD God asked a question.
He said, “Who told you that you were naked?”
The LORD God gave a command before.
He commanded the man not to eat from a certain tree.
The LORD God asked, “Have you eaten from the tree I commanded you not to eat from?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֚י הִגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עֵירֹ֖ם אָ֑תָּה הֲמִן־ הָעֵ֗ץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר צִוִּיתִ֛יךָ לְבִלְתִּ֥י אֲכָל־ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ אָכָֽלְתָּ׃

passages.text: And the man answered, “The woman whom You gave me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”
passages.sermon:
Adam was the first man.
God created Adam.
God placed Adam in the garden.
God gave Adam a woman to be with him.
Adam spoke to God.
Adam said, “The woman You gave to be with me gave me fruit from the tree.”
Adam said, “I ate the fruit.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י הִ֛וא נָֽתְנָה־ לִּ֥י מִן־ הָעֵ֖ץ וָאֹכֵֽל׃

passages.text: Then the LORD God said to the woman, “What is this you have done?” “The serpent deceived me,” she replied, “and I ate.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD God spoke to the woman.
He asked her, “What is this you have done?”
The woman answered Him.
She said, “The serpent deceived me.”
She said, “I ate.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאִשָּׁ֖ה מַה־ זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑ית וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה הַנָּחָ֥שׁ הִשִּׁיאַ֖נִי וָאֹכֵֽל׃

passages.text: So the LORD God said to the serpent: “Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and every beast of the field! On your belly will you go, and dust you will eat, all the days of your life.
passages.sermon:
The LORD God spoke to the serpent.
The LORD God is the Creator and Judge.
The LORD God said, "You have done this thing."
"You deceived the woman."
"Because you did this, I curse you."
"You are cursed more than all livestock."
"You are cursed more than every animal of the field."
"You will move on your belly."
"You will eat dust."
"You will do this all the days of your life."
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֥ים׀ אֶֽל־ הַנָּחָשׁ֮ כִּ֣י עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּאת֒ אָר֤וּר אַתָּה֙ מִכָּל־ הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה וּמִכֹּ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה עַל־ גְּחֹנְךָ֣ תֵלֵ֔ךְ וְעָפָ֥ר תֹּאכַ֖ל כָּל־ יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the serpent.
God said, “I will make you and the woman enemies.
Your descendants and her descendants will also be enemies.
Her descendant will crush your head.
You will strike his heel.”
passages.original: וְאֵיבָ֣ה׀ אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ ה֚וּא יְשׁוּפְךָ֣ רֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תְּשׁוּפֶ֥נּוּ עָקֵֽב׃ס

passages.text: To the woman He said: “I will sharply increase your pain in childbirth; in pain you will bring forth children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the woman.
God said He would greatly increase her pain in childbirth.
The woman would have pain when she gives birth to children.
The woman would desire her husband.
The husband would rule over the woman.
passages.original: אֶֽל־ הָאִשָּׁ֣ה אָמַ֗ר הַרְבָּ֤ה אַרְבֶּה֙ עִצְּבוֹנֵ֣ךְ וְהֵֽרֹנֵ֔ךְ בְּעֶ֖צֶב תֵּֽלְדִ֣י בָנִ֑ים וְאֶל־ אִישֵׁךְ֙ תְּשׁ֣וּקָתֵ֔ךְ וְה֖וּא יִמְשָׁל־ בָּֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: And to Adam He said: “Because you have listened to the voice of your wife and have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Adam.
Adam was the first man.
God said, “You listened to your wife.
You ate from the tree.
I commanded you not to eat from that tree.
Because you disobeyed, I curse the ground because of you.
You will work hard to eat from it.
You will toil all the days of your life.”
passages.original: וּלְאָדָ֣ם אָמַ֗ר כִּֽי־ שָׁמַעְתָּ֮ לְק֣וֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ֒ וַתֹּ֙אכַל֙ מִן־ הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּיתִ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֲרוּרָ֤ה הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּֽעֲבוּרֶ֔ךָ בְּעִצָּבוֹן֙ תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֔נָּה כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Both thorns and thistles it will yield for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Adam.
God said the ground is now cursed because of Adam’s sin.
The ground will grow thorns for Adam.
The ground will grow thistles for Adam.
Adam will eat the plants of the field.
passages.original: וְק֥וֹץ וְדַרְדַּ֖ר תַּצְמִ֣יחַֽ לָ֑ךְ וְאָכַלְתָּ֖ אֶת־ עֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread, until you return to the ground— because out of it were you taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Adam.
Adam was the first man.
God said Adam would work hard for food.
Adam would eat bread by the sweat of his brow.
Adam would do this all his life.
Adam would do this until he returned to the ground.
God made Adam from the ground.
Adam was taken from dust.
Adam is dust.
Adam will return to dust.
passages.original: בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֙יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל־ הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי־ עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל־ עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: And Adam named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living.
passages.sermon:
Adam was the first man.
Adam had a wife.
Adam gave his wife a name.
Adam named his wife Eve.
Eve would become the mother of all living people.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֧א הָֽאָדָ֛ם שֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ חַוָּ֑ה כִּ֛י הִ֥וא הָֽיְתָ֖ה אֵ֥ם כָּל־ חָֽי׃

passages.text: And the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and He clothed them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD God acted.
The LORD God made garments of skin.
Adam was the first man.
Eve was Adam’s wife.
The LORD God made these garments for Adam and his wife.
The LORD God clothed Adam and his wife with the garments.
passages.original: וַיַּעַשׂ֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְאָדָ֧ם וּלְאִשְׁתּ֛וֹ כָּתְנ֥וֹת ע֖וֹר וַיַּלְבִּשֵֽׁם׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...”
passages.sermon:
The LORD God spoke.
The LORD God saw Adam.
Adam was the first man.
Adam had eaten from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
The LORD God said, “Look, the man has become like one of Us.
He knows good and evil.
Now the man might reach out his hand.
He might also take fruit from the tree of life.
He might eat from it.
He might live forever.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים הֵ֤ן הָֽאָדָם֙ הָיָה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לָדַ֖עַת ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע וְעַתָּ֣ה׀ פֶּן־ יִשְׁלַ֣ח יָד֗וֹ וְלָקַח֙ גַּ֚ם מֵעֵ֣ץ הַֽחַיִּ֔ים וְאָכַ֖ל וָחַ֥י לְעֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: Therefore the LORD God banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.
passages.sermon:
The LORD God acted.
The LORD God banished Adam from the Garden of Eden.
Adam had lived in the Garden of Eden.
The LORD God sent Adam away.
Adam had been formed from the ground.
The LORD God sent Adam to work the ground.
Adam was to work the same ground from which he had been taken.
passages.original: וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֛הוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִגַּן־ עֵ֑דֶן לַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֻקַּ֖ח מִשָּֽׁם׃

passages.text: So He drove out the man and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life.
passages.sermon:
The LORD God acted.
The LORD God drove out the man from the Garden of Eden.
The LORD God placed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden.
The LORD God also placed a flaming sword that turned in every direction.
The cherubim and the flaming sword guarded the way to the tree of life.
passages.original: וַיְגָ֖רֶשׁ אֶת־ הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁכֵּן֩ מִקֶּ֨דֶם לְגַן־ עֵ֜דֶן אֶת־ הַכְּרֻבִ֗ים וְאֵ֨ת לַ֤הַט הַחֶ֙רֶב֙ הַמִּתְהַפֶּ֔כֶת לִשְׁמֹ֕ר אֶת־ דֶּ֖רֶךְ עֵ֥ץ הַֽחַיִּֽים׃ס
